title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In this sequence of pages Grothendieck works on the action of an outer-Galois-type automorphism u on profinite fundamental groupoids of the sphere minus three points, P^1 - {0,1,∞}. He uses base points adapted to the real structure, with complex conjugation τ as an involution. P^+ and P^- are base points in the upper and lower half-planes (the north and south poles in the sketch, with the real circle drawn as the equator). Q_i are base points on the three real intervals; R_i^ω are six further base points. The arrows d_i^ω run from P^ω to Q_i, crossing the real interval labelled i. The triples of arrows are torsors under 𝔖_3 = 𝔖_J, the symmetry group of {0,1,∞}.

This page, step by step.
(1) He restricts to the groupoid induced on the two vertices P^+ and P^- (the figure labelled IV_J). The composites d̃_i^ω = (d_i^{ω'})^{-1} d_i^ω, defined on the previous page, are three paths from P^ω to P^{ω'}, each crossing one real interval. This groupoid is described as the free groupoid on these arrows. The count checks out: three arrows between two vertices give π_1 of rank 3 - 2 + 1 = 2, i.e. the free group π_1(P^1 - 3 points). The arrows are parametrised simply transitively by 𝔖_J.
(2) An automorphism u fixing both vertices is then determined by formula (46): u(d̃_i^ω) = d̃_i^ω Ψ̃_i^ω(β̃). Here β̃ ∈ Π̂_{0,3} is a single element, independent of i and ω, transported to π(P^ω) by the identifications Ψ̃_i^ω : Π_{0,3} ≅ π(P^ω) (from (38), (43)).
(3) The only relations to impose come from d̃_i^{ω'} d̃_i^ω = 1. They yield (47): β̃ σ_∞(β̃) = 1, where σ_∞ is the involution of Π_{0,3} exchanging the loops around 0 and 1. This is exactly the shape of the 2-cycle relation f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1 of the later Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (Drinfeld 1990; Ihara). The previous page obtains β̃ = ξ σ_∞(ξ)^{-1}, for which the relation holds automatically.
(4) He then announces the next step. This is the groupoid induced on 11 base points (6 R_i^ω, 3 Q_i, 2 P^ω), built from arrows a, c, d with relations (48) and the conjugation τ (49), worked out on the following page.

Purpose. The page belongs to a program to describe the Galois / Grothendieck–Teichmüller action on Π̂_{0,3} with a 'Lego' of real-structure base points. The action is encoded by one parameter in Π̂_{0,3} subject to symmetry relations.
errors: Notation drifts. Formula (46) writes the transport map as φ̃/ψ̃_i^ω, whereas (43) uses Ψ̃_i^ω. Similarly, (47) is transcribed with τ_∞ where (44)-(45) use σ_∞. These look like the same involution and map, not genuinely different ones.

On this two-vertex groupoid the relation β̃σ_∞(β̃) = 1 is necessary. Whether it is sufficient for u to extend compatibly to the larger 11-vertex groupoid (the analogue of the 3-cycle relation) is not addressed here. It is deferred to the following pages.

ideas.what: Free fundamental groupoid of P^1 - {0,1,∞} on two base points (upper and lower half-planes), generated by the three real-interval-crossing paths, which form an 𝔖_3-torsor.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid with several (tangential or real-structure-adapted) base points; free groupoid presentation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984); Deligne 1989 for tangential base points; Ihara and Nakamura for Galois actions on groupoids
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses groupoids with base points stable under symmetries in general terms; this specific two-pole construction is not there to my knowledge

ideas.what: A base-point-fixing automorphism of the groupoid is determined by one element β̃ ∈ Π̂_{0,3}, subject to β̃σ_∞(β̃) = 1.
ideas.modern_name: Two-cycle relation f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1 of GT-hat
ideas.where_published: Esquisse only alludes to Teichmüller tower relations coming from M_{0,4} and M_{1,1}, without formulas

ideas.what: Using complex conjugation τ, which swaps the hemispheres P^±, to organise the base points. The parameter appears as β̃ = ξσ_∞(ξ)^{-1}, a 'coboundary' form.
ideas.modern_name: Real structure / complex conjugation in GT theory; the decomposition f = ξ σ(ξ)^{-1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara and others (complex conjugation in GT); Lochak–Schneps

missed.claim: The 2-cycle relation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group is derived from the groupoid on the two half-plane base points P^±, with the action parametrised by one β̃ ∈ Π̂_{0,3}. This predates Drinfeld's GT (1990).
missed.quote: Les seules relations à satisfaire correspondent aux équations d_i^{ω'}d_i^ω=1, qui donne (47) β̃ τ_∞(β̃)=1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is documentary evidence that Grothendieck explicitly had GT-type defining relations in his manuscripts. It bears on the history of GT-hat.

missed.claim: The base points are a real-structure-adapted cell-type 'Lego': the two hemispheres, the three intervals, and six more points, with τ acting. This is an alternative to tangential base points that the literature has explored little.
missed.quote: Considérons enfin le groupoïde induit sur les sommets R_i^ω, Q_i, P^ω (6+3+2=11 sommets)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give a combinatorial, τ-equivariant presentation of GT. That may be useful for real or dihedral variants of GT.

deep.surprise_reason: The page derives the GT 2-cycle relation pre-Drinfeld in a distinctive two-pole, real-structure framework. It is notable historically, but this kind of computation is widely assumed to have existed in Grothendieck's unpublished notes.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 '(ω≠ω̲)' is likely '(ω = ±)', i.e. the two signs ω ∈ {+,-}.
'avec paramètres de Γ̂_{0,3}' likely reads 'avec paramètres [en (-) correction] simplement transitif par 𝔖_J', meaning the d_i^ω form an 𝔖_J-torsor, consistent with the next page.
In (46) the factor is probably Ψ̃_i^ω(β̃), matching (43). 'indépendant de i, ω' under β̃ is likely correct.
In (47), σ_∞ is probably intended rather than τ_∞, consistent with (44)-(45).
Line 1 should read 'IV_J, groupoïde induit sur les deux sommets P^{+}, P^{-}', with 'fondamental' struck out.
